idiom_name: circe codecs (deriveCodec) for the wire form plus scala-jsonschema derivation for the published schema
implementation_notes: Scala's idiom is typeclass derivation: io.circe's Encoder/Decoder (semiauto deriveCodec rather than fully automatic) convert case classes to and from the JSON document, io.circe.parser.decode and Printer own the wire layer, and the published JSON Schema is derived from the same types with andyglow/scala-jsonschema (Json.schema[T]) so artifact and codecs cannot drift. Schema-first contracts use ScalaPB (protoc --scala_out) generated messages over the protobuf runtime. Hand-written codecs stay justified where the published shape is fixed by another party or differs from the domain types.
code_sketch:
import io.circe.*, io.circe.generic.semiauto.*, io.circe.syntax.*

final case class Order(id: Long, sku: String, qty: Int)
given Codec[Order] = deriveCodec[Order]

val wire: String = order.asJson.noSpaces          // the published JSON form
val in: Either[Error, Order] = decode[Order](body) // checked at the seam
// published artifact: Json.schema[Order].toJson (scala-jsonschema)
pitfalls: Automatic circe derivation hides missing codecs until runtime for nested types; semiauto/deriveCodec keeps contract gaps visible at compile time.
Default circe decoding ignores unknown fields - the tolerant behaviour a published language needs - so any stricter custom Decoder must be a deliberate compatibility decision.
ScalaPB messages are generated case classes: regeneration must run in the build, and the protobuf-java runtime version becomes a deployment-wide constraint across all participants.
